Finest reliable level of a code hierarchy

Source: R/share_intervals.R
finest_reliable_level.Rd

For every node, returns the node itself when its interval is narrow enough, otherwise the closest ancestor whose interval is.

Usage

finest_reliable_level(
  est,
  key_col,
  parent_col,
  rel_width_col,
  max_rel_width,
  level_col = NULL
)

Arguments

est

data.frame or data.table with one row per node.

key_col

Name of the node identifier column.

parent_col

Name of the parent column (NA or "" for roots).

rel_width_col

Name of the relative width column (e.g. (hi - lo) / quota); NA counts as not reliable.

max_rel_width

Maximum relative width of a reliable node.

level_col

Optional name of a level column; when given, the level of the reliable node is returned as well.

Value

A copy of est with column codice_affidabile (the node or its closest reliable ancestor, NA when none is reliable) and, when level_col is given, livello_affidabile.

Details

The search walks up the parent links one level at a time, vectorised over all nodes, and stops at the first node with rel_width <= max_rel_width.

Examples

est <- data.frame(
  code = c("A", "A1", "A11", "B", "B1"),
  parent = c(NA, "A", "A1", NA, "B"),
  level = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2),
  ampiezza_rel = c(0.1, 0.4, 1.2, 0.9, 2)
)
finest_reliable_level(est, "code", "parent", "ampiezza_rel", 0.5,
                      level_col = "level")
#>      code parent level ampiezza_rel codice_affidabile livello_affidabile
#>    <char> <char> <num>        <num>            <char>              <num>
#> 1:      A   <NA>     1          0.1                 A                  1
#> 2:     A1      A     2          0.4                A1                  2
#> 3:    A11     A1     3          1.2                A1                  2
#> 4:      B   <NA>     1          0.9              <NA>                 NA
#> 5:     B1      B     2          2.0              <NA>                 NA
